articles.title_original: 'Maxxing' selected as Dictionary.com word of the year
articles.title_zh: 'Maxxing' selected as Dictionary.com word of the year
facts_zh:
'Maxxing' selected as Dictionary.com word of the year
- Published
Americans have gone all in on "maxxing", making it the 2026 Word of the Year for Dictionary.com.

Short for maximising, the term "can be used on its own or added to the end of any word to convey you're doing something to the fullest or optimizing it as much as possible", Dictionary.com said in a statement.
It's a major departure from two years ago, when the site, after analysing US social media trends, news stories, and search data, chose demure as word of the year.

all_titles.en: 'Maxxing' selected as Dictionary.com word of the year

articles.title_original: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
articles.title_zh: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
facts_zh:
Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
- Published
Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office in a dramatic comeback over his right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.
Left-wing leader Lula took 51.79% of votes, becoming the first president since Brazil's return to civilian rule in 1985 to be elected after losing the first round of voting.
Lula told jubilant crowds his victory was a "loss for negativity, lies", adding "long live democracy".

all_titles.en: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback

articles.title_zh: Trump administration illegally fired James Comey's daughter, judge rules
facts_zh:
Trump administration illegally fired James Comey's daughter, judge rules
- Published
The US justice department illegally fired Maurene Comey, the daughter of former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) director James Comey, a federal judge has ruled.

Comey, who lost her job as a federal prosecutor in New York in July 2025, sued the government, arguing she was unlawfully fired because of her father, a critic of US President Donald Trump, and because of her perceived political affiliations.
Judge Jesse Furman ruled on Monday that the Trump administration must reinstate her and that she must be given back pay.

all_titles.en: Trump administration illegally fired James Comey's daughter, judge rules

Lula is the first candidate to win a runoff election after losing in the first round, taking victory with 51.79% of the vote to his rival’s 48.21%.

facts_zh:
Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973
- Published
Algeria is to send troops to Niger in its first foreign deployment since sending forces to Egypt during the Arab-Israeli war in 1973.
The deployment follows a visit to Algiers by Niger's defence minister, as the country seeks support against armed groups, some of which are linked to al-Qaeda or Islamic State.
Algeria has economic interests in Niger, including a planned gas pipeline that would carry Nigerian gas through Niger to Algeria.

Catholic bishops apologise for 'exploited' Trump meeting
- Published
Two Catholic bishops in the US have said they regret meeting President Donald Trump at the White House, after images of them praying with him were released and prompted many to ask if they were making a political statement.
Photos and video of the 22 October meeting show a group of bishops standing around Trump at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office.
Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, one of those pictured, said he had believed the meeting was private and not "a political photo opportunity".

Police have arrested a teenager in connection with a shooting on Saturday that injured 12 people in Florida.
The incident took place at 20:00 local time (01:00 Sunday GMT), close to an American football stadium in the city of Tallahassee where a university game had recently been played.
Eleven people were injured by gunfire, local police said, while another hurt their ankle while fleeing the scene.

articles.title_zh: Part of Antarctica named after former BBC science correspondent
facts_zh:
Part of Antarctica named after former BBC science correspondent
- Published
Part of Antarctica has been named after former BBC science correspondent Jonathan Amos.
A stretch of water between Rothschild Island and Alexander Island in the west of the White Continent is now called the Amos Channel.

Amos was given the honour for his "exceptional and influential role in bringing Antarctic research to the forefront of public understanding" during his 38-year career at BBC News, the naming committee said.

Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
- Published
Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to a student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections.
Celebrations erupted as crowds descended on the centre of Belgrade, Novi Sad and other cities.

The student movement was formed less than two years ago in response to a railway station disaster blamed on corruption and negligence, but fought the election with candidates from a cross-section of Serbian society.

Nurse killed in attack while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
- Published
A nurse has been killed and another health worker seriously injured in an attack as they were responding to an Ebola alert in north-eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The two were targeted by local youths who accused them of contaminating water sources and spreading the Ebola virus, according to the UN-backed Radio Okapi.
The World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the attack.

- Published
US singer Chris Brown has avoided jail after striking a man twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in a London nightclub.
The R&B star was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, over the attack at private members' club Tape in Mayfair, in the early hours of 19 February 2023.
Brown's vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who joined the attack, was sentenced to four months' imprisonment, suspended for 12 months.

facts_zh:
US Marine indicted for murder and robbery of woman in Japan
- Published
A US Marine has been indicted on suspicion of murdering and robbing a woman in Japan earlier this month in a case that has triggered protests, Japanese media reports.
Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, who was stationed at US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was arrested on suspicion of killing Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in Naha, the capital of Okinawa.
Prosecutors have now indicted him for allegedly strangling Yagi with a telephone cord and then stealing her backpack and wallet on 3 October, media reports, citing the indictment document.

facts_zh: Rapid Support Forces strike five power stations in three states controlled by Sudanese army Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces have launched a coordinated drone attack against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country’s east, a government official said.

The drones hit two power stations each in the states of Al-Jazira and Gedaref and one in White Nile state, “resulting in power outages across large parts of these three states”, the official said on condition of anonymity.
